summary: Before the roll is called: {the speaker} argues the bill in front of the chamber, and the player decides whether to stand with them, answer them, or sit still.
realLife: One life: On the Kentucky House floor a member addressed the Speaker and her colleagues against a symbolic gun bill, argued time was better spent on gun violence, cited a school shooting, and said she would vote no. Another: During debate in the Colorado House on a resolution about an amendment to the constitution, a member offered a limiting amendment and was told to keep remarks respectful. The next day another member answered on the floor, saying she was a colleague whether or not people accepted her; some opponents thanked her, the amendment failed and the resolution passed. Another: A Colorado House member used the floor's morning announcements to object to a colleague's remark, made at a forum, about his identity during a sanctuary debate. Chamber rules kept him from naming the colleague, who did not answer on the floor, and he closed by urging members to disagree without personal attacks.
gates: The bill record shows a bill on the floor with debate open and the roll not yet called.
The player is a member of {the body} with a seat in the room.
{the speaker} has been recognized by {chamber leader} and holds a stance on the bill on the stance record.
weights: How far apart the speaker and the player stand on the bill.
How close the vote is on the stance record.
Whether the player's district holds people the bill reaches.
Whether the debate has run long and members want it over.
How the speaker usually carries themselves in debate.
choices: stand with the speaker and say why
say you see it differently and give a reason
ask the speaker to yield for a question
say nothing and keep your seat

branches.when: the player stands with the speaker
branches.then: The player's stand is read into the debate record and by the speaker, who thanks them; the player's vote is now said aloud.

branches.when: the player says they see it differently
branches.then: The player's reasons go into the debate and the speaker answers; the exchange is read by members still deciding.

branches.when: the player asks the speaker to yield for a question
branches.then: The question is heard by the whole chamber; the speaker's answer is read as dodging or plain.
The silence is written; members who counted the player on either side adjust.
The chair or the presiding officer calls for decorum; the member who answers well or badly is read by the press.
